script.problem: It has 2 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.

terra.problem: Calling David a king adds a fact not stated in this psalm without a reference to another passage.
The oven-mitt joke does not make sense as a comparison: it is unclear why scary dough would make an oven mitt a place of refuge.
It states as fact that David is amazed, rather than marking that feeling as Papa Dorin's inference.
It states as fact that David is amazed, though the text does not name his feeling.
It presents wonder as David's certain feeling rather than as an inference.
The text does not say that David is not trying to defeat them himself.
It identifies those in verse 6 as David's enemies, although the verse leaves 'them' unidentified.
David says he will sing; the explanation says he stops to sing, presenting it as an action he is already taking.
It calls David a king without a reference for that fact, and describes the promised song as a thank-you, which the passage does not say.
The verse says the plants are nurtured in their youth, not that they are cared for from the start.
The verse says the pillars are carved to adorn a palace; it does not say they hold up the building or identify strength as part of the comparison.
No breach in the walls does not establish that there is no hole of any kind anywhere in them.
No going into captivity does not mean everyone stays home.
The picture of no captivity does not say that the people stay safe at home.
The reference to 'the drawer days' does not explain that Papa Dorin spent years in a drawer, so a baker unfamiliar with his story lacks the context.
It identifies the people David asks the LORD to scatter as his enemies, although verse 6 leaves 'them' unidentified.
